correctness.rationale: The finite counting-configuration space is Polish. A dense countable basis of open balls whose boundaries have zero mass for the sum of the two intensity measures yields nested finite partitions whose disjoint-count ℓ1 costs increase pointwise to signed-measure full variation. The coupling set with fixed marginals is weakly compact. Each finite-partition expected cost is lower semicontinuous because counts are almost surely continuous at zero-boundary configurations, and a Skorokhod coupling plus Fatou applies. Disintegration lifts every projected count-vector coupling, identifying finite minima with projected Wasserstein-1 distances. Nested closed sublevel sets and monotone convergence exchange the supremum of these minima with the infimum of the limiting full-variation cost and furnish an attaining coupling. The Hahn-Jordan formula K=max(positive mass,negative mass), D=sum proves sharp factor bounds, and a common-plus-residual Poisson coupling gives the exact intensity-variation formula.

originality.rationale: The directly motivating open-access full text introduces d_pi, proves only d_pi ≤ 2 d_KR, and explicitly leaves their equivalence unresolved. The new exact projective optimal-coupling identity supplies the missing reverse comparison and an attaining coupling; its Poisson intensity identity is an additional exact calibration. Published-record and mathematical-literature searches using both named metrics, count-vector Wasserstein/projective aliases, and signed full variation did not locate a covering result. General compactness arguments are classical and an abstract prior projective transport specialization remains an explicit residual risk.
residual_risks: An abstract published projective-limit optimal transport theorem may imply the equality via the present specialization even though no inspected point-process result states it explicitly.
The theorem is limited to finite-intensity point processes on Polish spaces; a general measurable-space extension needs separate justification.

value.rationale: The primary paper explicitly identifies metric equivalence as open, and the theorem resolves it with the optimal factor range 1 to 2 on all Polish state spaces. The exact optimal-coupling interpretation is structural rather than an isolated inequality, and the closed-form Poisson intensity-variation distance makes the metric useful for calibrating approximation bounds. The result does not rely on an arbitrary sliced parameter choice.
